question.stem: The nurse is providing care to a client recently diagnosed with advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma exhibiting cancer cachexia syndrome. Which metabolic and clinical manifestations should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass (sarcopenia) with or without loss of adipose tissue
Systemic chronic inflammation mediated by pro-inflammatory cytokines such as tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) and interleukin-6 (IL-6)
Marked anorexia, early satiety, and elevated basal resting energy expenditure
Complete reversal and restoration of lean body mass achieved solely through conventional caloric nutritional support
Profound asthenia, generalized physical weakness, and anemia of chronic disease
Hypertrophy of abdominal rectus muscles secondary to tumor-induced hyperinsulinemia

question.preamble: The palliative oncology nurse is conducting a comprehensive functional and nutritional assessment on a client with advanced malignancy.
question.explanation: Cancer cachexia is a multifactorial paraneoplastic wasting syndrome characterized by involuntary progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass (sarcopenia), profound asthenia, anorexia, anemia, and chronic systemic inflammation driven by tumor- and host-derived cytokines (TNF-alpha/cachectin, IL-1, IL-6, interferon-gamma) and lipid-mobilizing factors. Unlike simple starvation, which conserves lean muscle by burning adipose tissue and resolves with food intake, cancer cachexia accelerates muscle protein proteolysis via the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, elevates resting metabolic rate, and cannot be reversed by caloric intake alone.

leftContent.intro: A 66-year-old client with metastatic pancreatic cancer is assessed in the outpatient clinic. Over the past 4 months, the client has experienced an involuntary 18 kg (22%) weight loss, temporal muscle wasting, and severe weakness.

tabs.title: Nutritional & Clinical Assessment
tabs.content:
Anthropometrics: BMI 16.8 kg/m² (down from 23.4); temporal wasting, sunken clavicles, intercostal hollowing.
Inflammatory Markers: C-reactive protein (CRP) 48 mg/L (normal < 5 mg/L); Erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) 76 mm/hr.
CBC: Hemoglobin 8.6 g/dL (normocytic, normochromic); Albumin 2.4 g/dL.
